subject: Separating shared/specific/residual variances with known reliability

messages.author: 9065d041a7201790
messages.subject: Separating shared/specific/residual variances with known reliability
parts:
Hello everyone.

I am trying to figure our whether it might be possible to get a distinct estimate of the true specific and error variance for several indicators of a latent variable, if assuming that the reliabilities of these indicators are known. 
I have tried testing this using this model, but it constantly produces negative variance, so I must be missing something. Assume three known variables: one, two, three, with known reliabilities which can be converted to errors variance e1,e2,e3.

latent_g=~l_one+l_two+l_three
l_one=~1*one
l_two=~1*two
l_three=~1*three

one~~e1*one
two~~e2*two
three~~e3*three

Any help regarding how to proceed from here would be much appreciated!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Separating shared/specific/residual variances with known reliability
parts:
You cannot decompose any specific source of variance from measurement error unless there are multiple indicators of it.  Think of multitrait-multimethod CFA models, for example, or SEMs of generalizability theory from designs with > 2 facets.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Thanks, Terrence.

I see what you mean. The thing is that I can estimate the reliability of each indicator in a preceding stage. I would assume that if I have such an estimate, and have the indicators loading on a shared, latent, variable, I would be able to get an estimate of the specific variance. What is the core difference between having separate sub-indicators of an indicator (allowing to estimate measurement error), and specifying the measurement error manually in this case?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Separating shared/specific/residual variances with known reliability
parts: I can estimate the reliability of each indicator in a preceding stage

Reliable variance is just systematically repeatable components.  In the preceding stage, any shared variance that is in common among all the indicators will be considered part of the "true score" in classical test theory.  Their variance is reliable.  

If that holds across all 3 indicators at their preceding stages, then their reliable specific-error variance is retained in the composite, along with the construct variance of interest, rather than being proportionally minimized as indicator-specific measurement error is (even if that includes reliable specific variance unique that indicator).

So at the current stage, the same applies.  Any specific variance that is in common across the 3 composite indicators (whose reliabilities you estimated previously) will be confounded with the construct variance of interest.  Any specific variance that is unique to a composite will be confounded with that composite's other unique sources of (systematic and random) measurement error.

I would assume

Incorrectly (sorry), unless you have 3 separate estimates of the construct, specific-error, and random-error variances in each composite.
What is the core difference between having separate sub-indicators of an indicator (allowing to estimate measurement error), and specifying the measurement error manually in this case?

The difference is whether you have unique information about each source of variance to facilitate decomposing them in a model.  Hopefully you have access to this article to read: https://doi.org/10.1037/met0000107
Vispoel et al. (2018) provide a great discussion of reliability/generalizability in CTT, (C)FA, and GT.  Pay close attention to their interpretation of a one-facet design (e.g., multiple occasions to quantify test-retest reliability), in which random measurement error is confounded with any other source of systematic variance that was not part of the design (e.g., multiple items or raters).  A two-facet design can be used to decompose systematic error associated with both occasions and raters from random measurement error, the latter of which remains confounded with the occasion-rater interaction as well as any other systematic error not part of the design (e.g., multiple scale items or tasks).

It sounds like you have data that conform to a hierarchical CFA (lower-order factors indicate a higher-order factor), but are using composites as the indicators of the higher-order factor.  Perhaps you can model them altogether, and use semTools::reliabilityL2() to calculated reliability of the higher-order construct.  
Or you could conceive of the 3 composite indicators as 3 different measurement conditions, in each of which are nested different scale times.  That would give you a 2 (nested) facet GT design, or maybe a 2 crossed facet design if the scale items are conceptually parallel across the 3 composite indicators.  Then you could use a CFA of GT.  I provide lavaan examples for my open-access tutorial: 
https://osf.io/43j5x/

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
